title: First-fit warehouse bin packing
instructions:
Implement an incremental first-fit packer for integer item weights.

## Files
- `packing.py`

Public API:
- `validate_weights(weights, capacity: int) -> list[int]`: `weights` is an iterable.
  Capacity and every weight must have exact type `int` (reject bool). Capacity
  must be positive, and weights must be between 1 and capacity inclusive. Wrong
  types raise `TypeError`; invalid integer values raise `ValueError`. Validate
  capacity even for an empty iterable. Return a new list in input order.
- `BinPacker(capacity: int)` validates capacity by the same rules and starts empty.
- `add(weight: int) -> int`: put the item into the earliest existing bin with
  enough remaining capacity, or append a new bin. Return its zero-based index.
  Never reorder items or bins. Reject an invalid weight without modifying state.
- `add_many(weights) -> list[int]`: add in iterable order and return one bin index
  per item. Validate the entire iterable before adding anything, so an invalid
  item leaves all bins unchanged. An empty iterable returns `[]`.
- `snapshot() -> list[list[int]]`: return the bin contents in creation order with
  items in insertion order. Return a deep copy of the lists.
- `remaining() -> list[int]`: free capacity in each bin, in creation order, as a
  fresh list.
- `first_fit(weights, capacity: int) -> list[list[int]]`: convenience helper using
  a new packer and the same validation/packing rules. Empty input returns `[]`.
An exact fit is allowed. This is first-fit, so do not sort by weight or choose a
later bin simply because it would leave less spare capacity.
